tasks.description: Extract a tar, tar.gz or zip archive from a URL, host path or module file into a directory.
tasks.details:
Extracts a `.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tar` or `.zip` archive into `dest`.

```yaml
- archive.extract:
    src: https://example.com/tool-1.2.3-linux-amd64.tar.gz   # URL, absolute host path, or module file
    dest: /opt/tool
    strip_components: 1              # drop the archive's top-level directory
    include: ["tool", "LICENSE"]     # optional; exact names, `*` globs, or directory prefixes
    creates: /opt/tool/tool          # skip the task when this exists
    owner: root
    group: root
    mode: "0755"                     # applied to extracted files (not directories)
```

`src` is fetched over HTTP(S) when it starts with `http://` or `https://`,
read from the host when it is an absolute path, and otherwise read from the
module's `files/` directory. The archive format is detected from its
content, so unusual file names are fine.

Without `creates`, the plan compares every file in the archive with `dest`
and is a no-op only when they all match; for a URL that means downloading
the archive on every plan, so give remote archives a `creates:` path (which
may be relative to `dest`) to skip the work. `creates` must be produced by
the archive, or the task fails after extracting.

Entries that would land outside `dest` (absolute paths, `..`) are rejected,
as is writing beneath a symlink the archive itself created. The archive is
held in memory and may not expand beyond 1 GiB. Files keep the archive's
modes unless `mode` is set. A symlink entry never replaces an existing
file or directory (or a symlink Buckle did not create) unless
`force: true`; the plan is blocked instead.

Removal deletes the files Buckle extracted, and the directories it created
if they are then empty, but only if every file is still exactly as
extracted; otherwise it leaves everything in place. Files that were
already in `dest` before Buckle first extracted over them are not Buckle's
and are never deleted.

fields.description: Absolute directory to extract into (created if missing).
URL, absolute host path, or path relative to the module's `files/` directory.
Skip the task when this path exists (relative paths are relative to `dest`).
Let symlink entries replace existing files, directories or foreign symlinks.
Only extract entries matching one of these names, `*` globs or directory prefixes.
Octal mode such as `0644`, parsed from the string form in YAML.
Number of leading path components to drop from every entry.

tasks.description: Run a command, made idempotent with creates, unless, only_if and changed_when; secrets reach it through the environment.
tasks.details:
Runs a command, guarded so that it only runs when something needs doing.

```yaml
- command.run:
    run: ["nomad", "node", "eligibility", "-enable", "-self"]   # argv, or a string run with `sh -c`
    unless: "nomad node status -self -json | grep -q '\"SchedulingEligibility\": \"eligible\"'"
    creates: /var/lib/app/initialised     # skip when this path exists
    only_if: ["test", "-d", "/srv/data"]  # skip unless this exits 0
    changed_when: "output_contains:created"   # always | never | output_contains:<text> | exit:<code>
    env:
      API_TOKEN: "{{ secrets.api_token }}"  # secrets go through the process-environment sink
    cwd: /srv/app
    user: deploy                           # run as this account (runuser on Linux, sudo -u on macOS)
    timeout: 2m
    remove: ["rm", "-f", "/var/lib/app/initialised"]   # cleanup when the task leaves the config
    capture: redacted                      # redacted (default) | always | never
    identity:                              # a cluster credential in the environment
      cluster: home-nomad                  # a fleet.clusters target
      purpose: drain                       # read | deploy | drain (default)
      env: NOMAD_TOKEN                     # the variable it is passed in (default)
```

**Planning.** `creates` existing, `unless` exiting 0 or `only_if` exiting
non-zero all make the plan a no-op. The `unless` and `only_if` probes run in
plan mode too, so they must be read-only. A command with none of `creates`,
`unless` or `changed_when` is planned as `always runs: <command>` so the
author sees the smell; the plan of such a task is never a no-op.

**Applying.** The command runs and fails the task on a non-zero exit (except
when `changed_when: exit:<code>` names that code). `changed_when` decides
whether the run counts as a change for handlers: `always` (the default),
`never`, `output_contains:<text>` (stdout or stderr) or `exit:<code>`.

**Secrets.** An `env` value that references `secrets.` is rendered with the
real value and handed to the process through the environment sink; it is
never rendered into the plan, the logs or the state. When any env value is
secret, the command's output is not captured (nor shown in errors) unless
`capture: always` is set. By default (`capture: redacted`) stdout and stderr
are recorded on the task's tracing span, truncated to 4 KiB each; `never`
records nothing.

**Running as a user.** With `user`, the command, its probes and its cleanup
run as that account: through `runuser -u USER --` on Linux (util-linux; the
step is blocked while it is missing) and `sudo -u USER` on macOS. The
account's `HOME`, `USER` and `SHELL` are set as a login would set them; the
task's `env` is passed through. Windows does not support it.

**Removal.** With `remove`, the cleanup command runs when the task leaves
the configuration (in the same `cwd`, as the same `user`, with the
non-secret `env`). Without it the removal is reported as "no cleanup
defined".

**Cluster identity.** With `identity`, the agent asks the server for a
Buckle-issued identity for the cluster target and `purpose`, exchanges it
the way the cluster takes it (a Nomad ACL token through the `buckle` auth
method at `api`, else `NOMAD_ADDR`, else `http://127.0.0.1:4646`; the JWT
itself for Kubernetes) and passes it to the command and its probes in
`env`. It is treated as a secret: never planned, logged or stored, and
output is not captured unless `capture: always`. `drain` is granted to the
cluster's `nodes` only, `read` and `deploy` to its `executors`. The
cleanup command does not receive it. Local runs have no server to ask, so
the task fails there.

**Resource identity.** The resource is keyed by its rendered command, so editing the
command or a var inside it re-keys it (a removal plus an addition). Give a
templated command, or one with `remove`, a stable task `id`.

tasks.description: Manage a cron job as a Buckle-owned file in /etc/cron.d.
tasks.details:
Manages a cron job as its own file in `/etc/cron.d`.

```yaml
- cron.job:
    name: backup-nightly            # file name: letters, digits, '-' and '_' only
    user: root                      # default: root
    schedule: "30 2 * * *"          # five fields, or @hourly @daily @weekly @monthly @yearly @reboot
    command: /usr/local/bin/backup --quiet
    state: present                  # or absent
```

The file `/etc/cron.d/<name>` (mode 0644, root) is owned entirely by
Buckle. Unescaped `%` characters in `command` are escaped for you, because
cron would otherwise treat them as newlines. `command` must be one line.
Removal deletes the file if it still has the content Buckle wrote.

fields.description: `present` or `absent`, for kinds that can remove what they manage.

tasks.description: Pull a container image (missing or always, detecting digest changes), or remove it.
tasks.details:
Pulls a container image with Docker, or removes it.

```yaml
- docker.image:
    name: ghcr.io/example/profiler:1.4.0   # include the tag (or an @sha256 digest)
    pull: missing                           # missing (default) | always
    state: present                          # or absent
```

With `pull: missing` the image is pulled only when `docker image inspect`
cannot find it. With `pull: always` the image is pulled on every apply so a
moving tag such as `latest` is refreshed; the task is then reported as
changed only if the image's `RepoDigests` differ before and after the pull,
but because the registry is not consulted in plan mode it always appears as
a pending change in plans. Pin tags or digests where that is not wanted.

Requires `docker` on the PATH (reported as blocked when missing). Removal
runs `docker image rm` for an image Buckle pulled; an image still used by a
container is left in place. It holds the `docker` lock.

fields.description: `present` or `absent`, for kinds that can remove what they manage.

tasks.description: Ensure a file, symlink or directory does not exist.
tasks.details:
Ensures a file, symlink or directory does not exist.

```yaml
- file.absent:
    path: /etc/motd.d/10-legacy
    recursive: false      # required to delete a non-empty directory
```

A symlink is removed as a link and its target is left alone. A non-empty
directory is reported as blocked unless `recursive: true`. A recursive
delete is refused for `/`, for any top-level directory (`/etc`, `/var`,
`/home`, ...), for well-known system directories such as `/usr/lib` or
`/var/lib`, for a path containing `..`, and for a path that is empty or
has surrounding whitespace (the usual sign of a template that rendered
nothing). Because Buckle
deleted something that was not its own, there is nothing to undo when the
task is later removed from the configuration.

fields.description: Absolute path to delete.
Delete directories together with their contents.

tasks.description: Manage a marked block of lines inside a text file (blockinfile).
tasks.details:
Manages a block of lines between marker comments, like Ansible's `blockinfile`.

```yaml
- file.block:
    path: /etc/hosts
    marker: "# {mark} nomad cluster"      # {mark} becomes BEGIN / END
    block: |
      10.0.0.1 nomad-1
      10.0.0.2 nomad-2
    insert_after: '^127\.0\.0\.1'          # optional; default is the end of the file
```

The block, including its `BEGIN` and `END` marker lines, is inserted when
missing and rewritten in place when its content differs. `insert_after` and
`insert_before` take a pattern (the last match wins) or `EOF` / `BOF` and
only matter when the block is first inserted. With `state: absent` the
block and its markers are deleted. The file must exist unless
`create: true`; mode and ownership are preserved; `backup: true` keeps a
timestamped copy before each edit.

The marker lines delimit what Buckle owns, so removal deletes everything
between them, and a file Buckle created is deleted if that leaves it empty.
Two blocks in one file need different `marker`s. Edits of one file are
serialised across modules.

`validate` is a command (argv) that checks the new content before it
replaces the file (and while planning); `{path}` stands for a private
temporary copy under `<state_dir>/tmp`, deleted afterwards. A non-zero
exit fails the task and leaves the file untouched. Without `validate`,
`/etc/sudoers`, `/etc/sudoers.d/*` and `sshd_config` files are checked with
`visudo -cf {path}` and `sshd -t -f {path}` (when those tools are
installed); `validate: []` turns that off.

fields.description: Absolute path of the file to edit.
Keep a timestamped `.bak` copy before editing.
The lines of the block (may be empty, which leaves just the markers).
Create the file when it does not exist.
Insert after the last line matching this pattern, or `EOF`.
Insert before the last line matching this pattern, or `BOF`.
Marker line template containing `{mark}`.
`present` or `absent`, for kinds that can remove what they manage.

A command that checks the new content; `{path}` stands for the file to check.
Default: automatic for sudoers and sshd_config; `[]` disables.

tasks.description: Copy a file from the module's files/ directory to the host, with mode, owner and group.
tasks.details:
Copies a file from the module's `files/` directory to `dest`.

```yaml
- file.copy:
    src: nomad/client.hcl        # relative to the module's files/ directory
    dest: /etc/nomad.d/client.hcl
    mode: "0640"                  # optional; owner and group too
    owner: root
    group: nomad
    backup: true                  # keep a timestamped copy of the file being replaced
```

The file is written atomically. Plans show a unified diff for text files
and a digest change for binary ones. Removal deletes `dest` only if its
content still matches what Buckle wrote; otherwise it is left in place.

`validate` is a command (argv) that checks the new content before it
replaces the file (and while planning); `{path}` stands for a private
temporary copy under `<state_dir>/tmp`, deleted afterwards. A non-zero
exit fails the task and leaves the file untouched. Without `validate`,
`/etc/sudoers`, `/etc/sudoers.d/*` and `sshd_config` files are checked with
`visudo -cf {path}` and `sshd -t -f {path}` (when those tools are
installed); `validate: []` turns that off.

fields.description: Absolute destination path on the host.
Source path, relative to the module's `files/` directory.
Keep a timestamped `.bak` copy of the destination before replacing its content.
Octal mode such as `0644`, parsed from the string form in YAML.

A command that checks the new content; `{path}` stands for the file to check.
Default: automatic for sudoers and sshd_config; `[]` disables.

tasks.description: Ensure a directory exists with the given mode, owner and group (optionally recursively).
tasks.details:
Ensures a directory exists with the given permissions.

```yaml
- file.directory:
    path: /var/lib/nomad
    mode: "0750"
    owner: nomad
    group: nomad
    recurse: false
```

Missing parent directories are created too. With `recurse: true` the
permissions are also applied to everything already inside the directory
(the mode applies to files as well as directories, so prefer setting
`owner` and `group` when recursing). `recurse` is about permissions only.

Removal deletes the directory only if Buckle created it and it is empty
(files that other tasks wrote into it are removed by those tasks first,
since removals run in reverse order). Contents Buckle did not create, such
as the data a service keeps in `/var/lib/nomad`, are never deleted, and a
directory that existed before Buckle managed it is never deleted.

fields.description: Absolute path of the directory.
Octal mode such as `0644`, parsed from the string form in YAML.
Apply the permissions to existing contents as well (never affects removal).

tasks.description: Download a URL to a file, verifying a SHA-256 checksum, and write it atomically.
tasks.details:
Downloads a URL to `dest`, optionally verifying a SHA-256 checksum.

```yaml
- file.download:
    url: https://releases.example.com/tool-1.2.3-linux-amd64
    dest: /usr/local/bin/tool
    mode: "0755"
    checksum: "sha256:9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08"
    # or: checksum: https://releases.example.com/tool-1.2.3.sha256
    headers: { Authorization: "Bearer {{ secrets.release_token }}" }   # values may use secrets
    force: false
```

With `checksum`, the file is up to date when its SHA-256 matches, and the
download is verified before anything is written: a mismatch is an error and
leaves `dest` untouched. The checksum may be `sha256:<hex>`, a bare hex
digest, or the URL of a `.sha256` / `SHA256SUMS` file (the line naming the
downloaded file is used). Without `checksum`, an existing `dest` is
considered up to date and is never re-downloaded, unless `force: true`,
which downloads on every apply (and so always shows as a change).

The download is held in memory and written atomically. Removal deletes
`dest` only if its content still matches what Buckle wrote.

fields.description: Absolute destination path.
The URL to GET.
`sha256:<hex>`, a bare hex digest, or the URL of a file containing one.
Download again even if `dest` exists (when no checksum is given).

Extra request headers (also sent when fetching a checksum URL). Values
may reference secrets: `Authorization: "Bearer {{ secrets.token }}"`.
Octal mode such as `0644`, parsed from the string form in YAML.

tasks.description: Own settings and lines in one section of an INI-style file (config.txt, php.ini, .conf).
tasks.details:
Owns settings and lines in one `[section]` of an INI-style file, leaving the rest of it alone.

```yaml
- file.ini:
    path: /boot/firmware/config.txt
    section: all
    settings:                        # one value per key: replaced in place
      enable_uart: 1
      dtparam=poe_fan_temp0: 50000   # a key may itself hold `=`
    lines:                           # repeatable keys, kept as written
      - dtoverlay=rpi-poe-plus
      - dtoverlay=pps-gpio,gpiopin=18
    absent: [dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d]
```

`section` names the `[section]` header to edit (exactly as written, without
brackets); without it the task edits the lines before the first header.
A missing section is appended to the end of the file.

Each `settings` entry replaces the **last** line in the section that starts
with `key=` (whitespace around the separator is ignored), or adds
`key=value` when there is none. Each of `lines` is added unless an
identical line is already in the section. Lines that are already right are
adopted as they are. New lines are added together, settings first, after
the section's last line; later edits keep them where they are.

`absent` deletes lines from the section: an entry matches a line equal to
it, or one that starts with it followed by `=` or `,` (so `enable_uart`
matches `enable_uart=1` and `dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d` matches
`dtoverlay=vc4-kms-v3d,cma-512`). Lines the task itself wants are kept.
Comments (`#`, `;`) are never matched.

Buckle records what it changed. Dropping an entry from the task, or
removing the task, reverts it: added lines (and a section header Buckle
added) are deleted, replaced lines get their original text back and lines
deleted by `absent` are put back. Lines changed by hand since are left
alone.

The file must exist unless `create: true`, so a task for a file that only
some hosts have plans as blocked on the others. Mode and ownership are
preserved, and edits of one file are serialised across modules.

Lines to delete: an entry matches a line equal to it or followed by `=` or `,`.
Keep a timestamped `.bak` copy before editing.
Create the file when it does not exist.

The section to edit (`all` for `[all]`); omit for the lines before the first header.
What to write between a setting's key and value; `=` by default, ` = ` for spaced files.
Keys with a single value: `key: value` replaces the line starting with `key=` or adds one.

tasks.description: Ensure a line is present in, replaced in or removed from a text file (lineinfile).
tasks.details:
Ensures a line is present in (or absent from) a text file, like Ansible's `lineinfile`.

```yaml
- file.line:
    path: /etc/ssh/sshd_config
    line: "PasswordAuthentication no"
    regex: '^#?PasswordAuthentication\b'   # replace the last matching line

- file.line:                      # without `regex`: append when missing
    path: /etc/hosts
    line: "10.0.0.5 vault.internal"

- file.line:                      # remove every matching line
    path: /etc/fstab
    state: absent
    regex: '\sswap\s'
```

With `state: present` (the default): when `regex` matches, the **last**
matching line is replaced by `line`; when nothing matches, `line` is
inserted unless it is already in the file. Insertion goes after the last
line matching `insert_after` (or `EOF`), before the last line matching
`insert_before` (or `BOF`), and otherwise at the end of the file.

With `state: absent`, every line matching `regex` (or, without `regex`,
equal to `line`) is deleted.

The file must exist unless `create: true`. Mode and ownership are
preserved. `backup: true` keeps a timestamped copy before each edit.

`validate` is a command (argv) that checks the new content before it
replaces the file (and while planning); `{path}` stands for a private
temporary copy under `<state_dir>/tmp`, deleted afterwards. A non-zero
exit fails the task and leaves the file untouched. Without `validate`,
`/etc/sudoers`, `/etc/sudoers.d/*` and `sshd_config` files are checked with
`visudo -cf {path}` and `sshd -t -f {path}` (when those tools are
installed); `validate: []` turns that off.

Removal reverts the edit: a line Buckle added is deleted again (one
occurrence only, so an identical line another task owns stays), a line it
replaced is restored to its original text, and a file it created is deleted
when it ends up empty. Edits made by `state: absent` are not restored.

The resource is identified by `path` and `regex` when a `regex` is given
(else by `path` and `line`), so changing the `line` of a regex task updates
the same line in place and removal still restores the text from before
Buckle's first edit. Edits of one file are serialised across modules.

fields.description: Absolute path of the file to edit.
Keep a timestamped `.bak` copy before editing.
Create the file when it does not exist.
Insert after the last line matching this pattern, or `EOF`.
Insert before the last line matching this pattern, or `BOF`.
The line to ensure (required for `state: present`; must be a single line).
Pattern selecting the line to replace (present) or delete (absent).
`present` or `absent`, for kinds that can remove what they manage.

A command that checks the new content; `{path}` stands for the file to check.
Default: automatic for sudoers and sshd_config; `[]` disables.

tasks.description: Ensure a symbolic link exists and points at the given target.
tasks.details:
Ensures `path` is a symbolic link to `target`.

```yaml
- file.symlink:
    path: /usr/local/bin/nomad
    target: /opt/nomad/1.9.0/nomad
    force: true       # replace an existing file (or empty directory) at `path`
```

A symlink pointing elsewhere is always replaced. Anything else at `path`
blocks the plan unless `force: true`; `force` deletes a file but will not
delete a directory that has contents. Removal deletes the link if it still
points where Buckle pointed it.

fields.description: Absolute path of the link.
What the link points to (not required to exist).
Replace a regular file or empty directory found at `path`.

tasks.description: Render a template from the module's files/ directory (secret-aware) and write it to the host.
tasks.details:
Renders a template from the module's `files/` directory and writes the result to `dest`.

```yaml
- file.template:
    src: nomad/server.hcl.j2
    dest: /etc/nomad.d/server.hcl
    mode: "0640"
    owner: root
    group: nomad
    validate: ["nomad", "config", "validate", "{path}"]   # optional
    backup: false
```

Templates are rendered twice (design section 06): a redacted render, in
which secrets appear as `«secret:NAME@fingerprint»` tokens, is used for plan
previews and the state shadow; the real render is written through a file
sink and only its digest is kept. A plan therefore never contains a secret
value, and a rotated secret shows up as a fingerprint change on exactly the
lines that use it. When a file that contains secrets has drifted on disk,
the plan reports `content changed (digest a → b)` rather than a diff.

`validate` is a command (argv) run against the rendered content before it
replaces the destination (and while planning); `{path}` is replaced with a
private temporary file under `<state_dir>/tmp`, deleted afterwards. A
non-zero exit fails the task and leaves `dest` untouched. When the file
contains secrets, the validator's output is not echoed. Without
`validate`, `/etc/sudoers`, `/etc/sudoers.d/*` and `sshd_config` files are
checked with `visudo -cf {path}` and `sshd -t -f {path}` (when those tools
are installed); `validate: []` turns that off.

Removal deletes `dest` only if its content still matches what Buckle wrote.

fields.description: Absolute destination path on the host.
Template path, relative to the module's `files/` directory.
Keep a timestamped `.bak` copy of the destination before replacing its content.
Octal mode such as `0644`, parsed from the string form in YAML.

A command that checks the rendered file; `{path}` stands for the file to check.
Default: automatic for sudoers and sshd_config; `[]` disables.

tasks.description: Ensure tokens in a space-separated list on one line (cmdline.txt, GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX).
tasks.details:
Ensures tokens are present in (or absent from) a space-separated list on one line,
such as a kernel command line.

```yaml
- file.tokens:
    path: /boot/firmware/cmdline.txt
    present: [cgroup_enable=cpuset, cgroup_enable=memory, cgroup_memory=1]
    absent: [console=serial0]          # also matches console=serial0,115200

- file.tokens:                         # the quoted value of one assignment
    path: /etc/default/grub
    key: GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT
    present: [apparmor=1, security=apparmor]
```

Without `key`, the whole file is the list and must hold a single line (a
trailing newline is kept). With `key`, the list is the value of the last
`KEY=...` line (optionally `export`ed); its quotes are kept, and added when
the value grows past one token.

`present` tokens missing from the list are appended in order; tokens that
are already there stay where they are. `absent` deletes every token equal
to an entry, or starting with it followed by `=` or `,` (so `quiet` matches
`quiet`, `console` matches `console=tty1` and `console=serial0` matches
`console=serial0,115200`), except tokens listed in `present`.

Buckle records what it changed. Dropping a token from the task, or removing
the task, reverts it: appended tokens are deleted and deleted tokens are put
back where they were. A missing file (or `key` line) plans as blocked, so
the task can run on every host and changes only those that have the file.
Edits of one file are serialised across modules.

fields.description: Absolute path of the file to edit.
Tokens to delete: an entry matches a token equal to it or followed by `=` or `,`.
Keep a timestamped `.bak` copy before editing.
Edit the value of this `KEY="..."` assignment rather than the whole (single-line) file.
Tokens to ensure, appended when missing.

tasks.description: Copy a directory of files (optionally templated) from the module's files/ directory to the host.
tasks.details:
Copies every file under a directory of the module's `files/` to `dest`.

```yaml
- file.tree:
    src: compose                  # a directory under the module's files/
    dest: /opt/compose
    mode: "0640"                  # files; owner and group apply to directories too
    dir_mode: "0750"
    owner: root
    group: docker
    templates: true               # render `*.j2` files (secret-aware), dropping the suffix
    exclude: ["*.md", ".git"]     # globs over paths relative to `src` / `dest`
    purge: false                  # also delete files under dest that are not in the tree
```

The tree is one resource keyed by `dest`, and its plan shows a diff per
file. Buckle owns the files it writes: a file dropped from the module is
deleted on the next apply (or left in place, and reported, if it was
edited by hand since), and a hand-edited file that is still in the module
is reported as drift and overwritten. Directories Buckle created are
removed once empty. A file already on the host with the same content is
adopted rather than owned, so neither of those ever deletes it.

With `templates: true`, files ending in `.j2` are rendered like
`file.template` (secrets never reach the plan or state) and written without
the suffix; other files are copied byte for byte. With `purge: true`,
anything else under `dest` (that `exclude` does not match) is deleted as
well, so `dest` holds exactly the tree.

Removal deletes the files Buckle wrote that are unchanged since, then the
directories it created if they are empty.

fields.description: Absolute destination directory on the host (created if missing).
Source directory, relative to the module's `files/` directory (`.` for all of it).
Octal mode for `dest` and the directories in the tree, such as `"0755"`.

Skip paths matching these globs (`*` and `?`), matched against the
relative path, its parent directories and its file name.
Octal mode such as `0644`, parsed from the string form in YAML.
Also delete everything under `dest` that is not in the tree (and not excluded).
Render files ending in `.j2` as templates and write them without the suffix.

tasks.description: Clone a git repository and keep it at a branch, tag or commit, never resetting local changes.
tasks.details:
Clones a git repository and keeps its working tree at a branch, tag or commit.

```yaml
- git.repository:
    repo: https://github.com/geerlingguy/rpi-clone.git
    path: /opt/rpi-clone
    ref: master           # branch, tag or full commit id; default: the remote's default branch
    owner: pi             # run git as this user and own the tree
    group: pi
    depth: 1              # shallow clone/fetch
    recursive: true       # also init and update submodules
    update: true          # false: clone once, never move HEAD afterwards
  tags: [network]
```

The plan compares the checkout's `HEAD` with what `git ls-remote` reports
for `ref` on `repo`, so planning contacts the remote (a full 40 or 64
character commit id is compared without it). A branch is checked out as a
local branch tracking `origin/<ref>`; a tag or commit is checked out
detached. When `ref` names both a branch and a tag, the branch wins.

A working tree with uncommitted changes to tracked files is never reset:
a plan that would move `HEAD` is blocked instead. A non-empty `path` that
is not a git repository is blocked too. `owner` runs every git command as
that user (with `runuser`, so their SSH keys and git config apply) and
`owner`/`group` are applied recursively after each change.

Removal deletes the clone only if Buckle created it, it has no local
changes (tracked or untracked), and `HEAD` is still the commit Buckle last
checked out. Otherwise it is left in place.

fields.description: Absolute path of the working tree (created if missing).
The repository to clone: an https or ssh URL, or a path on the host.
Fetch only this many commits of history.
Group to own the working tree.
Run git as this user, and own the working tree.
Initialise and update submodules, recursively.
A branch, tag or full commit id. Defaults to the remote's default branch.
Move `HEAD` when the remote ref changes. `false` clones once and then leaves it alone.

tasks.description: Install a binary from a GitHub release, with arch mapping, version probe and checksum verification.
tasks.details:
Installs a binary from a GitHub release, upgrading it when a newer one appears.

```yaml
- github.release:
    repo: atuinsh/atuin
    version: latest                       # or "v18.3.0" / "18.3.0"
    asset: "atuin-{arch}-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz"  # {version} {arch} {os} {tag}
    arch_map: { x86_64: x86_64, aarch64: aarch64 }   # host arch -> asset arch; armv7l is skipped
    extract: atuin                        # file inside an archive asset
    dest: /usr/local/bin/atuin
    mode: "0755"
    probe: ["atuin", "--version"]         # prints the installed version
    probe_regex: 'atuin (\S+)'            # optional; default is the first x.y.z found
    checksum_asset: "atuin-{arch}-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz.sha256"
    token_env: GITHUB_TOKEN               # optional; name of an environment variable
```

The plan compares the version printed by `probe` with the wanted release
(`1.2.3 → 1.2.4`). `arch_map` extends the defaults `x86_64: amd64` and
`aarch64: arm64`; a host architecture with no mapping is reported as
blocked rather than failing, so a fleet can include hosts a release does not
support. `{os}` is `linux`, `darwin` or `windows`; `{version}` has no
leading `v`.

`version: latest` asks the GitHub API for the newest release on every plan,
which is rate limited to 60 requests an hour without a token; set
`token_env` to the name of an environment variable holding a token (the
value is only ever sent as an `Authorization` header). A pinned version
whose `probe` already reports it needs no API call. Without `probe`, an
existing `dest` counts as installed and is never upgraded (unless
`checksum_asset` is given for a plain binary asset).

Archive assets (`.tar.gz`, `.tgz`, `.tar`, `.zip`) need `extract`: the
path or file name of the binary inside. With `checksum_asset` (the name of a
`.sha256` or `SHA256SUMS` asset) the downloaded asset is verified before
anything is written. With `probe`, an install that does not then report the
release's version fails and puts the previous binary back, so an asset that
cannot run on the host (e.g. a glibc build on an older glibc) is reported
rather than reinstalled on every rollout. Removal deletes `dest` only if it
still matches what Buckle installed.

fields.description: Asset file name; may use `{version}`, `{tag}`, `{arch}` and `{os}`.
Absolute path to install the binary at.
`owner/name` of the repository.
Host architecture (as `uname -m` prints it) to the asset's spelling; extends the defaults.
Name of a SHA-256 checksum asset in the release; may use the same placeholders as `asset`.
For archive assets: the binary's path or file name inside the archive.
Octal mode such as `0644`, parsed from the string form in YAML.
Command (argv) that prints the installed version.
Regular expression selecting the version from the probe's output (first capture group, else the match).
Name of an environment variable holding a GitHub token.
`latest`, `vX.Y.Z` or `X.Y.Z`.

tasks.description: Set the machine's hostname (live and in /etc/hostname).
tasks.details:
Sets the host's name, both live and in `/etc/hostname`.

```yaml
- hostname.set:
    name: "{{ host.id }}"
```

The plan compares the running (kernel) hostname and `/etc/hostname` (when
it exists) with `name`; when they disagree with each other the change
shows both. Applying runs `hostnamectl set-hostname` (falling back to
`hostname` when `hostnamectl` is missing or cannot reach systemd, as in a
container) and rewrites `/etc/hostname`. With neither tool installed the
plan is blocked.
`name` must be a valid hostname: letters, digits and `-`/`.`, at most 253
characters. Removal does nothing: Buckle does not know what the previous
hostname should be, so a hostname is released rather than reverted.

tasks.description: Manage public keys in a user's ~/.ssh/authorized_keys with correct permissions.
tasks.details:
Manages public keys in a user's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.

```yaml
- ssh.authorized_key:
    user: deploy
    key: |
      ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nza... laptop
      from="10.0.0.0/8" ssh-ed25519 AAAAC3Nza... ci
    state: present        # or absent
    exclusive: false      # true: the file contains exactly these keys
```

`key` is one or more lines in `authorized_keys` format (blank lines and
`#` comments are ignored). A key is identified by its type and base64
body, so changing its options or comment updates the existing line rather
than adding a second one. With `state: absent` the listed keys are deleted.
With `exclusive: true` (and `state: present`) every other key is deleted.

The `.ssh` directory is kept at mode 0700 and the file at 0600, owned by the
user (and by their private group when one with the user's name exists). If
the user does not exist yet (an earlier task creates it) the plan assumes
`/home/<user>` (`/root` for root). Removal deletes the key lines Buckle
added and leaves the rest of the file, including an emptied file, alone.

fields.description: One or more public key lines.
Remove every key not listed (only with `state: present`).
`present` or `absent`, for kinds that can remove what they manage.

tasks.description: Create a swap file, add it to fstab and activate it; one resource owns all three.
tasks.details:
Creates and activates a swap file, and makes it permanent.

```yaml
- swap.file:
    path: /swapfile
    size_mb: 2048
    swappiness: 10        # optional; sets vm.swappiness live and persistently
```

One resource owns the file, its `/etc/fstab` line and the `swapon` state:
the plan is a no-op when `/proc/swaps` lists the file at the right size, the
fstab entry exists, the file is mode 0600 and swappiness matches. Applying
creates the file (`fallocate`, or `dd` where that fails), sets mode 0600,
runs `mkswap`, adds `<path> none swap sw 0 0` to `/etc/fstab` and runs
`swapon`. A file of the wrong size is swapped off and recreated. Swappiness
is applied with `sysctl -w vm.swappiness=N` and persisted in
`/etc/sysctl.d/99-buckle-swap.conf`.

An existing file at `path` that is not an active swap area is only
recreated or formatted (`mkswap`) when Buckle created it or it already
carries a swap signature; anything else (a data file at the wrong path) is
reported as blocked and left untouched.

Removal runs `swapoff`, deletes the fstab line and the file, but only for a
swap file that Buckle created. It holds the `fstab` lock.

fields.description: Absolute path of the swap file.
Size in MiB.

tasks.description: Set a kernel parameter live and persist it in /etc/sysctl.d.

fields.description: The sysctl key, e.g. `vm.swappiness`.
The value to set (a string, number or boolean).
The file to persist into; defaults to `/etc/sysctl.d/90-buckle-<module>.conf`.
Also write the setting to a sysctl.d file so it survives reboots.

tasks.description: Reboot the host once the run has finished (a handler, or a task guarded by only_if).
tasks.details:
Reboots the host after the run.

```yaml
handlers:
  reboot:
    system.reboot:
      delay: 5s          # wait after the run has been reported (default 5s)
      timeout: 10m       # how long a rollout waits for the host to come back (default 5m)

tasks:                   # or as a task, guarded so it only reboots when needed
  - system.reboot: { only_if: "test -f /run/reboot-required" }
```

The task never reboots in the middle of a run. Applying it asks for a
reboot; the run carries on through every module, handler and removal, and
the host reboots once, after the run has been reported (to the server, or
on screen for `buckle apply`). Health checks the run had not reached when
the reboot was asked for run after the reboot instead, as part of the bake.
In a rollout the host shows as rebooting, and fails only if its agent has
not reconnected from a new boot within `timeout`.

A drift correction never reboots on its own; the reboot it asked for is
logged and left to the next apply or to an operator.

Without `only_if` the task plans a change on every run, so as a task (not a
handler) it would reboot the host on every apply: plans flag it.

fields.description: How long to wait after the run has been reported, e.g. `5s`.
Reboot only when this read-only probe exits 0. Runs in plan mode too.
How long a rollout waits for the host to come back, e.g. `5m`.

tasks.description: Ensure a local user account exists with the given uid, groups, shell, home and password hash.
tasks.details:
Ensures a local user account exists with the given attributes (or is absent).

```yaml
- user.account:
    name: sierra
    uid: 1001                      # optional
    group: sierra                  # primary group (must exist)
    groups: [sudo, docker]         # supplementary groups, appended (never removed)
    shell: /bin/bash
    home: /home/sierra
    create_home: true              # default: true, or false for `system: true`
    system: false                  # a system account (useradd -r)
    comment: "Sierra Softworks"
    password: "{{ secrets.sierra_password_hash }}"   # a crypt(3) hash, not plaintext
    state: present                 # or absent
    remove_home: false             # with state: absent, or when removed from the config
```

Uses `useradd`, `usermod` and `userdel`. Only the attributes you set are
compared and changed; `groups` are added with `usermod -a -G` and never
removed. A `password` is a pre-hashed value (`openssl passwd -6`) and may
reference secrets: it is applied with `chpasswd -e`, which receives
`name:hash` on **stdin** (through the secret sink), so it never appears on
a command line, in the plan or in logs. The plan compares the hash with
`/etc/shadow` by digest; if the shadow file cannot be read the password is
assumed to be correct.

Removing the task from the configuration deletes the account (`userdel`,
with `-r` only when `remove_home: true`) if Buckle created it, and is
flagged as a cautionary removal.

fields.description: Create the home directory; defaults to true except for system accounts.
Primary group.
Supplementary groups to be a member of.
A password hash (crypt format); may be a template referencing secrets.
Delete the home directory together with the account.
`present` or `absent`, for kinds that can remove what they manage.

tasks.description: Ensure a local group exists with the given gid, or is absent.
tasks.details:
Ensures a local group exists (or is absent).

```yaml
- user.group:
    name: nomad
    gid: 4646          # optional
    system: true       # a system group (low gid)
    state: present     # or absent
```

Uses `groupadd`, `groupmod` and `groupdel`. Removal is flagged as a
cautionary change: when the task leaves the configuration the group is
deleted, but only if Buckle created it.

fields.description: `present` or `absent`, for kinds that can remove what they manage.
